answer: Erasure-coded data availability sampling requires every active account to store a unique 64 GB Reed-Solomon coded state shard on local ferrous disks and serve random 16-chunk proofs whenever the epoch beacon pulses. Running 1,000 fake identities across a shared grove of cloud servers forces an operator to provision >= 64,000 GB of dedicated fast storage and lock 500,000 POA in bond, while one honest agent stores 64 GB once and locks 500 POA. Any account that misses a sample loses 100% of its bond, though an attacker with cheap bulk storage can still rent disk capacity.
